sourceRefs.locator: PAS FindID 147193, HESH-E20370, image 203021. The PAS description, photograph and scale identify the Long Cross type modelled on Æthelred II, moneyer Faeremin, Dublin mint and Shropshire findspot. Record date field 1000–1010; image description, author and CC BY-SA 4.0 credit on the file page.

British Numismatic Journal 78, p. 116 table 1 and pp. 122–124. First Irish issues in the 990s and their English prototypes; p. 124 and notes 65–68 distinguish English dies used in Dublin and Hiberno-Scandinavian-style dies at York.
“Viking coinage” and preceding paragraph. The museum puts the earliest Dublin pennies under Sihtric at around 997 or 998; English and other coins were circulating earlier.
The rulers of Dublin and mid-tenth-century York, chronology; Mark Blackburn’s chapter on the coinage, pp. 335–336, fig. 82.2, raven issue of Óláfr/Amlaíb Guthfrithsson in 939–941.

labels.en: A penny of the moneyer Faeremin

note.de: Der in Shropshire gefundene Penny HESH-E20370 wird dem Dubliner Münzmeister Faeremin zugeschrieben und in die Jahre um 1000–1010 eingeordnet. Die Karte zeigt den Prägeort Dublin, der genaue Werkstattstandort ist unbekannt.
note.en: Penny HESH-E20370, found in Shropshire, is attributed to the Dublin moneyer Faeremin and dated to about 1000–1010. The map marks the mint town. The location of the workshop is unknown.
